name: Americas Region Countries
description: The americas region in business refers to the geographic area encompassing north, central, and south america, and often includes the caribbean. companies operating on a global scale divide their operations into regions for more effective management, resource allocation, and strategic planning. the americas region is significant for businesses as it represents a diverse and substantial market with varying economic strengths, consumer behaviors, and regulatory environments.
sql: select region from application.countries where region like '%Americas%'

name: Backorder IDs
description: Backorders refer to customer orders for products that are currently out of stock but will be fulfilled once the inventory is replenished. they indicate strong demand and can help in forecasting future inventory needs, but excessive backorders may signal supply chain inefficiencies. managing backorders effectively is crucial to maintaining customer satisfaction and optimizing inventory turnover.

name: Faulty Goods Credit Notes
description: Faulty goods refer to products that are defective or do not meet the quality standards promised by the manufacturer or retailer. These items can lead to customer dissatisfaction, returns, and potential financial losses for the business. Efficient handling of faulty goods is crucial for maintaining customer trust and minimizing negative impacts on the companys reputation and bottom line.

name: Fleet Vehicle Count
description: In business, a fleet refers to a collection of vehicles owned or leased by a company and used for commercial purposes. The role of a fleet can vary from facilitating the delivery of goods and services to customers, to providing transportation for employees, or enabling the execution of specialized tasks such as construction or field service operations. Effective fleet management is crucial for optimizing operational efficiency, controlling costs, and ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.
sql: select count(distinct (vehicleregistration)) as fleetcount from warehouse.vehicletemperatures

name: Annual Supplier Purchase Totals By Year
description: This analysis provides a yearly breakdown of total purchases made from each supplier, allowing businesses to assess and compare the amount spent with different suppliers over time. It aids in identifying spending trends and evaluating supplier relationships based on the volume of purchases. The data can be instrumental in strategic decision-making regarding negotiations, procurement planning, and cost management.
sql: select extract(year from po.orderdate)::int as year, s.suppliername, sum(pol.expectedunitpriceperouter * pol.receivedouters) as total_purchased from purchasing.purchaseorders po join purchasing.suppliers s on po.supplierid = s.supplierid join purchasing.purchaseorderlines pol on po.purchaseorderid = pol.purchaseorderid group by extract(year from po.orderdate)::int, s.suppliername order by year, s.suppliername

name: Buying Group Order Counts
description: This SQL query is designed to provide a report on the number of orders associated with each buying group by counting the orders for each distinct buying group name. It joins the orders table with the customers table to link orders to customers, and then with the buying groups table to associate customers with their respective buying groups. The result will help the business understand the distribution of orders across different buying groups, which can inform sales strategy, marketing efforts, and customer relationship management.
sql: select bg.buyinggroupname, count(o.orderid) as order_count from sales.orders o join sales.customers c on o.customerid = c.customerid join sales.buyinggroups bg on c.buyinggroupid = bg.buyinggroupid group by bg.buyinggroupname

name: Cold Room Temperatures Log
description: This analysis retrieves a log of temperature readings from cold storage areas within a warehouse, including unique identifiers for each temperature record, the date and time when each temperature was recorded, and the actual temperature values. It is essential for ensuring that products stored in cold conditions are maintained at appropriate temperatures to meet safety and quality standards. The data can also be used to monitor the performance of cooling systems and to identify any irregularities or potential equipment failures.
sql: select crt.coldroomtemperatureid, crt.recordedwhen, crt.temperature from warehouse.coldroomtemperatures crt

name: May 2023 Invoices
description: This SQL query retrieves a list of invoice IDs, customer IDs, and invoice dates from a database table named invoices within the sales schema. It specifically filters the records to only include those where the invoice date falls within the month of May in the year 2023. This information can be used by the business to analyze sales performance, track billing cycles, or manage customer accounts for that particular month.
sql: select invoiceid, customerid, invoicedate from sales.invoices where extract(year from invoicedate)::int = 2023 and extract(month from invoicedate)::int = 5

name: Monthly Sales Summary By Invoice Date
description: This SQL query is designed to provide a monthly sales report for a business by aggregating the total sales of chiller and dry items from the invoices. It groups the sales data by month, ensuring that each month's total sales are calculated separately. The results are then ordered chronologically, allowing the business expert to easily analyze sales trends over time.
sql: select to_char(i.invoicedate, 'yyyy-mm') as month, sum(i.totalchilleritems) + sum(i.totaldryitems) as totalsales from sales.invoices i group by to_char(i.invoicedate, 'yyyy-mm') order by month

name: Monthly Sales Totals By Year
description: This SQL query is designed to provide a business expert with a monthly sales report, broken down by year. It calculates the total sales for each month by summing up the extended price from the invoicelines table within the sales schema. The results are grouped by year and month, and then ordered chronologically, allowing the business expert to analyze sales trends over time.
sql: select extract(year from lasteditedwhen)::int as year, extract(month from lasteditedwhen)::int as month, sum(extendedprice) as total_sales from sales.invoicelines group by extract(year from lasteditedwhen)::int, extract(month from lasteditedwhen)::int order by year, month

name: Order Details With Customer Names
description: This analysis provides a detailed view of orders by combining order information with customer names. It enables the business to track orders more effectively and understand customer purchasing patterns. This is essential for customer relationship management and targeted marketing efforts.
sql: select o.orderid, o.orderdate, c.customername from sales.orders o inner join sales.customers c on o.customerid = c.customerid

name: Order Details With Special Deals
description: This SQL query retrieves order details, including the order ID, order date, special deal descriptions, and discount amounts. It joins the orders with their respective order lines and any special deals associated with the items in those order lines. This information is crucial for analyzing the impact of special deals on sales and customer orders.
sql: select o.orderid, o.orderdate, sd.dealdescription, sd.discountamount from sales.orders o left join sales.orderlines ol on o.orderid = ol.orderid left join sales.specialdeals sd on ol.stockitemid = sd.stockitemid

name: Order Details with Stock Item Names
description: This sql query retrieves detailed information about orders, including the order id, order date, order line id, and the name of the stock items associated with each order. it joins the orders, order lines, and stock items tables to provide a comprehensive view of each order and its corresponding items. this information is crucial for analyzing sales performance and inventory management.
sql: select o.orderid, o.orderdate, ol.orderlineid, si.stockitemname from sales.orders o join sales.orderlines ol on o.orderid = ol.orderid join warehouse.stockitems si on ol.stockitemid = si.stockitemid

name: Supplier Transactions With Supplier Names
description: This sql query retrieves a list of supplier transactions, including each transactions unique id, the date of the transaction, and the name of the supplier. it joins two tables: one containing the transactions and the other containing the suppliers, matching them by the supplier id to provide a comprehensive view of transactions with their corresponding supplier names. this information is crucial for tracking purchases, analyzing supplier activity, and managing accounts payable within a business.
sql: select st.suppliertransactionid, st.transactiondate, s.suppliername from purchasing.suppliertransactions st join purchasing.suppliers s on st.supplierid = s.supplierid

name: Total Discount By Deal Description
description: This sql query is designed to calculate the total discount amount provided for each special deal across all sales orders. it does this by joining the order line items with the special deals based on the stock item id, then multiplying the quantity of each item sold by its unit price and the discount amount associated with the special deal. the results are grouped by the deal description, providing a clear summary of the financial impact of discounts offered through special deals.
sql: select sd.dealdescription, sum(ol.quantity * ol.unitprice * sd.discountamount) as total_discount from sales.orderlines ol join sales.specialdeals sd on ol.stockitemid = sd.stockitemid group by sd.dealdescription

name: Invoice Total Line Price
description: The total line price attribute is crucial in calculating the profitability of individual sales transactions. it represents the total revenue generated from a single line item on an invoice or sales order, which is essential for determining gross profit by subtracting the cost of goods sold. this attribute directly impacts the overall profit analysis by contributing to the revenue side of the profit equation.

name: Customer Delivery Geography
description: Maps each customer to delivery-based geography (country and continent) using the delivery city relationship (CUSTOMERS.DELIVERYCITYID → CITIES → COUNTRIES). Enables continent-level filters such as "Africa" to be applied during SQL construction without hardcoding conditions.
sql: select cust.customerid, ci.cityid, sp.stateprovinceid, c.countryid, c.countryname from sales.customers cust join application.cities ci on ci.cityid = cust.deliverycityid join application.stateprovinces sp on sp.stateprovinceid = ci.stateprovinceid join application.countries c on c.countryid = sp.countryid

name: Customer Postal Geography
description: Maps each customer to postal/home geography (country and continent) using the postal address path (POSTALCITYID → STATEPROVINCES → COUNTRIES). Use when the question implies customer origin rather than delivery location.
sql: select cust.customerid, ci.cityid, sp.stateprovinceid, c.countryid, c.countryname from sales.customers cust join application.cities ci on ci.cityid = cust.postalcityid join application.stateprovinces sp on sp.stateprovinceid = ci.stateprovinceid join application.countries c on c.countryid = sp.countryid

name: Product Total Sold Units
description: Aggregates the total units sold per stock item per customer by joining orders with order lines. Use when the question asks about product sales volume, units sold, or order quantities by product.
sql: select o.customerid, ol.stockitemid, sum(ol.quantity) as unitssold from sales.orders o join sales.orderlines ol on o.orderid = ol.orderid group by o.customerid, ol.stockitemid
